items.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports partial indexes
items.content_snippet: Amazon Aurora DSQL now lets you build an index over a specific subset of a table, storing only qualifying rows rather than every row in the entire table, which improves query performance and lowers index storage cost. Many tables hold a small working set alongside a much larger history, such as open orders among years of completed ones. Add a WHERE clause to CREATE INDEX to index just that working set. items.title: Your LLM App Returned 200 OK. It Was Still Wrong. — Marina Petzel, Datadog
items.content_snippet: Latency, errors, traffic and saturation tell you your app is up. They don't tell you if it's right. items.title: YOLO Mode, Safely: MicroVM Sandboxes for Any Agent — Rowan Christmas, Docker
items.content_snippet: Rowan tried to hack himself with his own coding agent. Five prompts later it had found his browser history, his bank accounts and more. Rowan Christmas, product manager at Docker, shows why harness-level guardrails aren't enough to protect your machine from your own agent, and how microVM sandboxes give you security by design. items.title: The 5 Levels of Self-Driving Production — Eric Schwartz, Traversal
items.content_snippet: Coding agents made development faster. They also made production a lot harder to debug. Eric Schwartz, product manager at Traversal, explains why more AI-written code means more time spent troubleshooting, why observability dashboards tell you what broke but not why, and why root cause analysis is a causal problem rather than an observability problem. items.title: Lessons from Generating 12 Trillion Synthetic Tokens — Bogdan Gaza, DatologyAI
items.content_snippet: The web has roughly 30 trillion tokens of usable text. Frontier pre-training needs more. Here's how DatologyAI generates the rest. Bogdan Gaza, co-founder and CTO of DatologyAI, shares the engineering lessons from running synthetic data jobs at trillion-token scale, including a recent run of about 12 trillion tokens across web, math and code. items.title: Why AI Didn't Actually Make You Ship Faster — Gabriel Spencer-Harper, Meticulous
items.content_snippet: AI writes code faster than humans can review it. Verification is now your bottleneck. Gabriel Spencer-Harper, co-founder and CEO of Meticulous, explains why assertion-based tests can't keep up with AI-generated code, and what near-exhaustive frontend verification with zero developer effort looks like. items.title: Why 99% Accurate Browser Agents Still Fail — Derek Meegan, Browserbase
